names.name: Hanson Gregory
names.said: Claimed the hole and told it the same way for sixty years.

text.what: The New England sailor who said he punched the first hole in a donut in 1847, at sixteen, aboard a lime-trading ship.
text.story:
Gregory said he disliked how greasy twisted donuts were and how raw their centres came out, and punched a hole through the middle with the ship's tin pepper box, later teaching his mother the trick. The Smithsonian's account has his mother, Elizabeth Gregory, frying a deep dough that used his spice cargo — nutmeg, cinnamon, lemon rind — and putting hazelnuts or walnuts in the middle where the dough might not cook through.

The claim is one of several. Michael Krondl suggests the ring came from recipes for a jumble, a ring-shaped cookie; Linda Civitello writes the hole made donuts cook faster. By 1870 a cutter with two concentric circles was in production.
text.today: Nobody has produced a document that settles it, and the story is repeated as settled anyway.

kin.as: The other Gregory in the story.
